title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 3 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Composite Number Classification' test, in contrast to prime classification?
options: Whether a group of numbers are all composite, with one being prime (breaking the pattern)
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all even
Whether numbers are all perfect cubes
questions.rationale: Composite number classification tests whether a group of numbers are all composite, identifying the one number that is actually prime.

questions.question: What does 'Perfect Square Classification' test?
options: Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all odd
Whether a group of numbers are all perfect squares (n^2), with one number not being a perfect square
Whether numbers are all composite
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers are all perfect squares, identifying the one number that is not a perfect square and breaks the pattern.

questions.question: In the set 4, 9, 16, 20, 25, which number is the odd one out under Perfect Square Classification?
questions.rationale: 4, 9, 16, and 25 are all perfect squares (2^2, 3^2, 4^2, 5^2); 20 is not a perfect square.

questions.question: What does 'Perfect Cube Classification' test?
options: Whether numbers are all perfect squares
Whether numbers are all even
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether a group of numbers are all perfect cubes (n^3), with one number breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers are all perfect cubes, identifying the one that is not a perfect cube.

questions.question: What does 'Multiples Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of numbers are all multiples of some common number, with one not being a multiple of it
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
Whether numbers are all odd
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers are all multiples of a shared base number, identifying the one that isn't.

questions.question: What does 'Divisibility Classification' test, similarly?
options: Whether numbers share a common digit sum
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether a group of numbers are all divisible by some common number, with one not being divisible by it
Whether numbers are all perfect cubes
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers is all evenly divisible by a specific number, identifying the exception that isn't.

questions.question: What does 'Digit Sum Classification' test?
options: Whether numbers are all prime
Whether a group of numbers share a common digit sum, with one number having a different digit sum
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
Whether numbers are all even
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers all share the same digit sum (e.g., all sum to 9), identifying the one number whose digits sum to something different.

questions.question: What does 'Digit Product Classification' test, in contrast to digit sum?
options: The same property as digit sum
Whether a group of numbers share a common digit product, rather than a common digit sum
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all odd
questions.rationale: This tests a shared digit PRODUCT (multiplying the digits together) rather than a digit sum, identifying the number whose digit product differs.

questions.question: What does 'Number of Factors' classification test?
options: A shared digit sum
Whether a group of numbers all have the same count of factors, with one number having a different count
A shared prime status
A shared perfect-square status
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of numbers all have the same total number of factors, identifying the one number with a different factor count.

questions.question: What does 'Prime Position Classification' test?
options: Whether numbers are all prime
Whether a group of numbers occupy prime-numbered positions in some sequence, with one not doing so
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
Whether numbers share a digit sum
questions.rationale: This tests whether a set of numbers occupy positions in a sequence that are themselves prime numbers, identifying the one that doesn't.
